Rating notch change (Watchlist POC — one task)

Source: POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md (Corporate Client Credit Monitoring — Watchlist Tool).
This job is a one-requirement slice of that document: the notch change that Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the notch
calculator (REQ-06-02) are built on. It is small: one card.

## Requirement

| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-06-02 (part) | Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them | BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0 |

## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)

- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+").
- C2. Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object
  such as `new String('A')` is a non-string. No banking-regulation or internal-policy constraint applies to this slice.
- C3. The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.
- C4. No UI, CLI or printed output; other parts of the POC import the function.

## Contract

- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).

Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

## Staffing

- The backend developer works on the **haiku** model.

dl — the deterministic half of the /deliver flow.
The board, phase transitions, worktrees, gates, reviews and merges are run by this script, not by the LLM.
Michael (the orchestrator) calls these commands through Bash; you can call them from a terminal too.
Every transition is checked here: a model cannot skip a gate, merge an unreviewed card or exceed the limits.

  dl [-C <repo>] <command> …     -C (or DELIVER_REPO) = run against that repo from any directory

  dl new "<title>" "<request>"   new job: .work/<JOB>/, job/<JOB> branch, integration worktree
  dl status                      active job's phase + board table + next actions
  dl next                        the next actions the flow requires, one per line (ACTION args)
  dl board                       board table only
  dl phase <phase>               set phase (intake readiness awaiting_clarification planning awaiting_plan_approval executing
                                 integrating closing awaiting_pr_merge done aborted) — guarded
  dl jobset '<jq expr>'          update job.json            e.g. dl jobset '.stack=["typescript","react"]'
  dl readiness                   check the requirements readiness review (readiness.json → readiness.md, QUESTIONS.md)
  dl clarify <id> "<answer>"     record the human's answer to an open business question (human only)
  dl decide <id> "<decision>" "<rationale>"   the PM closes an open implementation-detail item (owner pm)
  dl unfreeze "<reason>"         (human, terminal only) reopen the decisions frozen at planning
  dl reseal "<reason>"           (human, terminal only) accept an edit made to job.json/board.json outside dl
  dl roles                       check job.roles against roles.yaml and generate the project's role cards
                                 (.work/<job>/roles/*.md, ROLES.md) — runs on dl phase planning
  dl learn <role|all> "<lesson>" --topic <slug> (--card T-xx | --evidence "…") [--scope project|shared|kit]
                                 propose a lesson, with what happened; it reaches .deliver/knowledge/ with this job's PR
  dl followup "<finding>" [--card T-xx]   a defect seen outside the job's scope — listed in the PR
  dl knowledge [list|topics|promote <topic> "<rule>"|sync-md]   standards + lessons for the role cards; promote = a new
                                 standard (with the PR); sync-md → Munder Difflin knowledge graph
  dl validate                    board.json schema + dependency + scope-overlap check
  dl ready                       ids of cards that may be dispatched now (deps merged, attempts left)
  dl wt add <card> [--resume]    card worktree + state=running + attempts+1 (--resume: no bump, after a restart)
  dl wt rm <card>                remove the card worktree (branch is kept)
  dl card <card> state <state>   review | blocked | ready (from blocked) | archived ["<reason>" — required after the start]
  dl card <card> note "<text>"   attach a note to a card (blocked reason, guidance, …)
  dl reopen <id> "<why>"         before the freeze: an answer that does not answer its question goes back to the human
  dl pm-decide "<what>" "<why>" [card]   after the start the human is not asked: your decision, logged, listed in the PR
  dl card <card> retry           human-granted: attempts=0 and state=ready (after guidance)
  dl card <card> set <field> <value> "<reason>"   change a ready/blocked card's contract (validated, logged, history)
  dl card add <card.json> "<reason>"              add a card (e.g. a fix card) — gets the next id, validated, logged
  dl gate <card>                 mechanical gate: right branch, clean tree, commits, in scope, verify passes
  dl qa <card> pass|fail "<summary>"   record the QA/Test verdict on the card's acceptance criteria
                                 (needs a passed gate on the current commit)
  dl review <card> approve|changes "<summary>" [--by <role>]   record a reviewer's verdict (needs gate PASS + QA pass);
                                 a card with "reviewers": [...] needs every one of them to approve the same commit
  dl integrate <card>            --no-ff merge into the job branch → merged (needs gate PASS + QA pass +
                                 review approve, all on the current commit; exit 3 on conflict, 5 when the
                                 repo's commit rules refuse the merge message)
  dl verify-all                  run verify_full in the integration worktree
  dl ship                        deliver per merge_mode: human|semi|auto → push + PR (+ auto-merge / merge on green),
                                 local → merge into the base branch. Needs verify-all PASS + report.md (phase closing)
  dl pr                          PR state (awaiting_pr_merge): merged → done; closed → aborted; open → checks/review
  dl approve plan [note]         record the human's plan approval (only when gates.plan is on; off by default)
  dl reject  plan "<note>"       record the human's rejection of the plan
  dl md-dispatch <card> <prompt-file>   Munder Difflin: run the card's dev as a worker on the floor
  dl md-hire                     Munder Difflin: seat one person per role seat (job.roles[].count) — the whole job
  dl md-seats                    who sits where: pending / starting / live / gone / failed (with why), each seat's open task
  dl config [--init]            the settings that apply in this repo (kit defaults ⊕ ~/.deliver/config.json ⊕ .deliver.json)
  dl floor-open "<request>"     /deliver from a terminal in a floor repo: open Munder Difflin on its floor, hand Michael the job
  dl dispatch munder|subagent "<why>"   (human) switch how this job's roles run: floor seats (default) or subagents
  dl md-reseat <seat> "<why>" [--model m]   a failed or stuck seat gets a new person (another model for a credit error);
                                 also spelled dl md-hire --reseat <seat>
  dl md-send <seat|role> <task> <prompt-file> [--agent a]   a work order to a seat: role card + agent instructions + task

# Role: ba — Business analyst

Job: **JOB-20261005-2151-rating-notch-change** — Rating notch change
Agent: `business-analyst` · runs on: claude · writes files: no
Why this role is on the job: always

## Mission

Turns the request into a traceable plan (Given/When/Then ACs), writes a spec for every card, checks the ACs at closing.

## Rules

1. You work on exactly one job. Your input is the prompt you were given plus the files it names; nothing else is assumed.
2. Never run state-changing dl commands (new, phase, roles, wt, card, gate, qa, review, integrate, ship, learn, cleanup). Michael owns the flow.
3. Push only your own card branch (never main/master, never the job branch, never force); never delete .work/ or job/* branches; never write in the main checkout.
4. Answer in exactly the output format the prompt asks for. Put details in files (handoff, plan), not in your reply.
5. If something is unclear and it changes scope, say so under open questions / open issues. Do not guess scope.
6. Analysis only: do not write code or tests and do not modify files. Return the plan, the card specs or the closing check as text.
7. Every acceptance criterion is numbered (AC-1, AC-2, …), traces to a requirement ID or a stated clarification, and is a Given/When/Then with concrete values.
8. Cover the edges: boundaries, invalid input, error paths, empty values — say what must happen.
9. Write Out of scope explicitly. Ask only open questions whose answer changes the scope.
10. When the request contradicts itself, name the contradiction and the resolution you assume.
11. A card spec covers every AC the card claims and nothing outside the card's scope.

## This project

- Repository: /tmp/claude-0/live/k050/models/repo (base branch main; job branch job/JOB-20261005-2151-rating-notch-change)
- Stack: node
- Full verification of the job: `npm test`
- Commits: no AI attribution — no 'Co-Authored-By: Claude …', no 'Generated with Claude Code', no Anthropic e-mail (the gate rejects them).
- Commits: `<CARD-ID>: <what changed>` (QA: `<CARD-ID> QA: <what>`).
- Project conventions: read `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root before you start.


## Company standards and memory

No standards are registered for this role yet (see docs/08-knowledge.md to add them).
======
Rating notch change (Watchlist POC — one task)

Source: POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md (Corporate Client Credit Monitoring — Watchlist Tool).
This job is a one-requirement slice of that document: the notch change that Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the notch
calculator (REQ-06-02) are built on. It is small: one card.

## Requirement

| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-06-02 (part) | Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them | BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0 |

## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)

- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+").
- C2. Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object
  such as `new String('A')` is a non-string. No banking-regulation or internal-policy constraint applies to this slice.
- C3. The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.
- C4. No UI, CLI or printed output; other parts of the POC import the function.

## Contract

- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).

Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

- The backend developer works on the **haiku** model.

summary:
# Plan

## Goal

Add one pure, synchronous function that gives the signed number of notches between a previous and a current credit rating on the 19-step scale in C1. A downgrade is positive, an upgrade is negative and no change is 0 (C3). Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator will be built on it later. The work is done when every AC below passes and `npm test` exits 0 (PRD-goal).

## Scope

- A new module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` with two named exports (Contract, X-module-shape):
  - `RATING_SCALE`: the 19 ratings from C1, best first, frozen with `Object.freeze`.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: returns the integer `index(current) - index(previous)`, from -18 to +18 (CON-interface, C3).
- Input handling (C1): each argument is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and matched without regard to case.
- Rejection (C2, CON-errors, X-scale-bounds, X-error-message): every invalid argument throws a `RangeError`. That covers unknown ratings, empty or whitespace-only strings, and anything that is not a string primitive, including `new String('A')`.
- JSDoc on `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange`. It states the sign convention and the RangeError (DEL-docs).
- Unit tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, written with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, run by `npm test` (TST-strategy, CLAUDE.md).
- Component: ratings-lib (library, node). Paths `src/ratings/` and `test/ratings/`, owner backend, reviewed by reviewer. One card.

## Out of scope

- The rest of REQ-06-02: the notch calculator itself, thresholds and how a notch change maps to a WL.
- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, and any WL calculation.
- Ratings outside the 19 C1 values: CC, C, D, SD, RD, NR, WD, Moody's or Fitch notation such as `Baa1`, outlook or watch suffixes, and rating-agency mapping. All of these are invalid input and are rejected; none is supported (X-scale-bounds).
- UI, CLI, logging, console output or any other I/O (C4, CLAUDE.md).
- Persistence, history or rating time series, and dates (ARC-data).
- Locale-aware case folding and normalising look-alike characters (for example U+2212 `−` to `-`).
- README or changelog updates (DEL-docs).
- New npm dependencies, lint, type checking and coverage tooling (ARC-stack, DEL-ci).
- A specific RangeError message text. Only the error type is part of the contract (C2, X-error-message).

## Acceptance criteria

Scale indices, best first: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.

QA can check each AC with `node --input-type=module -e "import {RATING_SCALE, notchChange} from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'; …"` run from the repo root, or with `npm test`.

**The REQ-06-02 examples**

- **AC-1 (REQ-06-02):** Given a previous rating of `'BBB+'` and a current rating of `'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+', 'BB+')` is called, then it returns `3` (a 3-notch downgrade, positive per C3).
- **AC-2 (REQ-06-02):** Given a previous rating of `'BB+'` and a current rating of `'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+', 'BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3` (a 3-notch upgrade, negative per C3).
- **AC-3 (REQ-06-02, C3, CON-interface):** Given the same rating twice, when `notchChange('A', 'A')` is called, then it returns positive zero: `Object.is(notchChange('A','A'), 0) === true` and `Object.is(notchChange('A','A'), -0) === false`. The same holds for `('AAA','AAA')` and `('CCC-','CCC-')`.

**The scale**

- **AC-4 (C1, Contract, X-module-shape):** Given the module is imported, when `RATING_SCALE` is read, then:
  - it deep-equals `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`;
  - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`;
  - `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true`;
  - `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`.
- **AC-5 (X-module-shape):** Given the module is imported, when a caller tries `RATING_SCALE.push('D')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'` or `RATING_SCALE.reverse()` in ESM (strict) code, then each throws a `TypeError`. After those attempts, `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3`.
- **AC-6 (X-module-shape, Contract):** Given `import * as m from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, when its exports are listed, then `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`, `m.RATING_SCALE` is the array from AC-4, and `'default' in m === false`.

**Every pair of valid ratings (C1 + C3)**

- **AC-7 (REQ-06-02, C1, C3):** Given any i and j from 0 to 18, when `notchChange(RATING_SCALE[i], RATING_SCALE[j])` is called, then it returns exactly `j - i`. The result is a number primitive with `Number.isInteger` true, never a Promise, NaN or undefined. All 361 pairs must hold. Concrete checks:

  | previous | current | expected |
  |---|---|---|
  | `'AAA'` | `'CCC-'` | `18` |
  | `'CCC-'` | `'AAA'` | `-18` |
  | `'AA+'` | `'AA'` | `1` |
  | `'A-'` | `'BBB+'` | `1` (crosses the letter group) |
  | `'BBB-'` | `'BB+'` | `1` (investment grade to sub-investment grade) |
  | `'BB+'` | `'BBB-'` | `-1` |
  | `'B-'` | `'CCC+'` | `1` |
  | `'AAA'` | `'AA+'` | `1` |
  | `'CCC'` | `'CCC-'` | `1` |
  | `'A'` | `'BBB'` | `3` |

**Normalisation (C1)**

- **AC-8 (C1):** Given lower-case or mixed-case input, when the function is called, then case is ignored:

  | previous | current | expected |
  |---|---|---|
  | `'bbb+'` | `'bb+'` | `3` |
  | `'Bb+'` | `'bBb+'` | `-3` |
  | `'aaa'` | `'ccc-'` | `18` |
  | `'a'` | `'A'` | `0` |

- **AC-9 (C1):** Given input with leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes, when the function is called, then the whitespace is ignored:

  | previous | current | expected |
  |---|---|---|
  | `' BBB+ '` | `'BB+'` | `3` |
  | `'\tbb+\n'` | `'  BBB+'` | `-3` |
  | `'\u00A0A\u00A0'` (non-breaking space) | `'A'` | `0` |
  | `'\uFEFFAAA'` | `'AA+'` | `1` |

- **AC-10 (C1, C2):** Given whitespace that `trim()` keeps, or that sits inside the rating, when the function is called, then it throws `RangeError`:
  - `notchChange('\u200BA', 'A')` (zero-width space, which `trim()` does not remove);
  - `notchChange('BBB +', 'A')`;
  - `notchChange('A', 'B B')`.

**Invalid input (C2, CON-errors, X-scale-bounds)**

In every row of AC-11 to AC-13 the error must be a `RangeError`: `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`, and the thrown error must not be a TypeError or any other type.

- **AC-11 (C2, X-scale-bounds):** Given a string that is not one of the 19 ratings after trimming and upper-casing, when it is passed as either argument, then `RangeError` is thrown. Values to check as `previous` (with `current = 'A'`) and as `current` (with `previous = 'A'`):
  - `'D'`, `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'SD'`, `'NR'`, `'WD'`
  - `'AAA+'`, `'A++'`, `'Baa1'`
  - `'BBB+ (neg)'`, `'BBB+u'`
  - `'BBB−'` (U+2212 minus sign)
  - `'BBB‐'` (U+2010 hyphen)
- **AC-12 (C2):** Given an empty or whitespace-only string, when it is passed as either argument, then `RangeError` is thrown. Values: `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, `'\u00A0'`.
- **AC-13 (C2):** Given a value that is not a string primitive, when it is passed as either argument, then `RangeError` is thrown. Values:
  - `undefined`, `null`, `3`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`
  - `{}`, `[]`, `['A']` (its `String()` is `'A'`, but it must still be rejected)
  - `new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`
  - `Symbol('A')`, `10n`, `() => 'A'`
  - missing arguments: `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')`
- **AC-14 (C2, CON-errors):** Given both arguments are invalid, when the function is called, then `RangeError` is thrown. Values: `notchChange('X', null)` and `notchChange('', '')`. The request does not say which argument is reported.

**Error message (X-error-message)**

- **AC-15 (X-error-message):** Given an invalid argument whose string conversion would itself throw, when the function is called, then the thrown error is still a `RangeError`, not a TypeError from building the message. Values:
  - `notchChange(Object.create(null), 'A')`
  - `notchChange('A', Symbol('x'))`
  - `notchChange({ toString() { throw new Error('boom') } }, 'A')`

  For `notchChange('D', 'A')` the message is a non-empty string that contains `previous`. For `notchChange('A', 'D')` it contains `current`. QA checks the message by inspection; unit tests assert only the error type, per X-error-message.

**Behaviour and conventions (C4, CLAUDE.md, Contract)**

- **AC-16 (C4, ARC-async, CLAUDE.md "no I/O"):** Given the module is imported, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` and `notchChange('D','A')` (caught) are called, then:
  - nothing is written to stdout or stderr. Running `node --input-type=module -e "import {notchChange} from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'; notchChange('BBB+','BB+'); try{notchChange('D','A')}catch{}"` produces empty output and exits 0;
  - the return value is synchronous (`typeof result === 'number'`);
  - `src/ratings/notch.mjs` imports no `node:` I/O module (`fs`, `http`, `process`, `console`).
- **AC-17 (Contract, ARC-stack, CLAUDE.md):** Given the finished change, when the repo is inspected, then:
  - `package.json` has no `dependencies` or `devDependencies` keys;
  - the module file is `src/ratings/notch.mjs`;
  - its tests are in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and cover AC-1 to AC-15;
  - `npm test` exits 0.
- **AC-18 (DEL-docs):** Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when it is read, then `RATING_SCALE` and `notchChange` each have a JSDoc block. The `notchChange` block states that a downgrade is positive, an upgrade is negative, no change is 0, and that invalid input throws `RangeError`. README.md is unchanged.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Resolved: test location.** The request says tests go "next to the code under `test/`". This is resolved by PRD-conflicts and CLAUDE.md as `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, not `src/ratings/`.
- **Resolved: RangeError for non-strings.** C2 deliberately asks for `RangeError` where JavaScript usually throws `TypeError`. It is binding (PRD-conflicts). A simple `typeof` guard that throws TypeError would fail AC-13 and AC-15.
- **Assumption: case-insensitive means `toUpperCase()`, not `toLocaleUpperCase()`.** Locale-aware folding (for example Turkish dotted/dotless i) is out of scope. No rating contains a letter affected by it.
- **Assumption: "trimmed" means exactly what `String.prototype.trim()` removes.** That includes NBSP and BOM (AC-9) and excludes the zero-width space U+200B (AC-10). This is stated in C1.
- **Assumption: extra arguments are ignored.** For example, `notchChange('A','A','x')` returns `0`. The request does not cover it and it changes no contract.
- **Assumption: validation order is not part of the contract.** When both arguments are invalid, only the error type is fixed (AC-14).
- **Risk: Node 18 support.** CLAUDE.md requires Node 18+, but the local runtime is v22.22.0. Using APIs newer than Node 18 (for example `Array.prototype.toSorted`, `Object.groupBy`) would pass locally and break on 18. The reviewer should check for this.
- **Risk: test discovery.** `npm test` runs bare `node --test`, which discovers `test/**/*.mjs`. A test file outside `test/` or with another extension would silently not run. QA should confirm the test count in the output is not 0.
- **Risk: edge cases the developer may miss.** The developer runs on the haiku model, so these traps are called out explicitly in the ACs:
  - `-0` versus `+0` (AC-3);
  - `['A']` and `new String('A')` passing a loose check (AC-13);
  - a message builder that throws on a Symbol or a null-prototype object (AC-15);
  - mutating the shared `RATING_SCALE` (AC-5).
- **Assumption: the 361-pair matrix in AC-7 is generated from the literal scale in AC-4 by a loop in the test.** The test must not derive it from the implementation's own lookup alone, so AC-4 pins the literal list.

## Open questions

None. Readiness has 0 open items, and nothing in the request leaves scope undecided.

5	## Goal
6	
7	Add one pure, synchronous function that gives the signed number of notches between a previous and a current credit rating on the 19-step scale in C1. A downgrade is positive, an upgrade is negative and no change is 0 (C3). Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator will be built on it later. The work is done when every AC below passes and `npm test` exits 0 (PRD-goal).

12	  - `RATING_SCALE`: the 19 ratings from C1, best first, frozen with `Object.freeze`.
13	  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: returns the integer `index(current) - index(previous)`, from -18 to +18 (CON-interface, C3).
14	- Input handling (C1): each argument is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and matched without regard to case.
15	- Rejection (C2, CON-errors, X-scale-bounds, X-error-message): every invalid argument throws a `RangeError`. That covers unknown ratings, empty or whitespace-only strings, and anything that is not a string primitive, including `new String('A')`.

# T-01: Add src/ratings/notch.mjs (RATING_SCALE + notchChange) with unit tests

## User story
As a developer of Indicators 11–13 and of the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want a pure, synchronous `notchChange(previous, current)` and a frozen `RATING_SCALE` that I can import from `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, so that I get the signed number of notches between two credit ratings (downgrade positive, upgrade negative, no change 0) without writing my own scale lookup.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-18 of plan.md. Requirements: REQ-06-02, C1, C2, C3, C4, Contract. Readiness: CON-interface, CON-errors, X-scale-bounds, X-module-shape, X-error-message, ARC-async, ARC-stack, DEL-docs, TST-strategy, PRD-conflicts.

Clarifications this spec relies on (none of them changes scope):
- **Imports (AC-16).** The plan says the module "imports no `node:` I/O module". The card is stricter: the module imports nothing. This spec uses the stricter rule, which also satisfies AC-16.
- **Error message (AC-15).** X-error-message fixes only the error type. The integration test may assert that the message is a non-empty string containing `previous` or `current`. Neither unit tests nor integration tests may assert the exact message text.
- **Invisible characters (AC-9, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12).** The plan shows them as literal characters. Here they are written as escapes: `\u00A0` NBSP, `\uFEFF` BOM, `\u200B` zero-width space, `\u2212` minus sign, `\u2010` hyphen. Test sources must use the escapes.
- **"npm test exits 0" (AC-17).** QA checks this on the command line. The integration test must not run `npm test` or a bare `node --test`, because it would start itself again in a loop.

## Acceptance criteria
Scale indices, best first: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18. Every `-` in a rating is ASCII U+002D.

1. AC-1 (REQ-06-02): Given previous `'BBB+'` and current `'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3`.
2. AC-2 (REQ-06-02): Given previous `'BB+'` and current `'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3`.
3. AC-3 (REQ-06-02, C3, CON-interface): Given the same rating twice, when `notchChange('A','A')`, `notchChange('AAA','AAA')` and `notchChange('CCC-','CCC-')` are called, then each result has `Object.is(result, 0) === true` and `Object.is(result, -0) === false`.
4. AC-4 (C1, Contract, X-module-shape): Given the module is imported, when `RATING_SCALE` is read, then it deep-equals `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`. The expected list is a literal written out in the test, not read from the module.
5. AC-5 (X-module-shape): Given ESM (strict) caller code, when it runs `RATING_SCALE.push('D')`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = 'X'` and `RATING_SCALE.reverse()`, then each throws `TypeError`. Afterwards `RATING_SCALE[0] === 'AAA'`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3`.
6. AC-6 (X-module-shape, Contract): Given `import * as m from '../../src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, when its exports are inspected, then `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`, `m.RATING_SCALE` deep-equals the AC-4 literal (and `m.RATING_SCALE === RATING_SCALE` from the named import), and `('default' in m) === false`.
7. AC-7 (REQ-06-02, C1, C3): Given every i and j in 0..18 over the literal AC-4 list, when `notchChange(list[i], list[j])` is called, then `assert.strictEqual(result, j - i)` holds, `typeof result === 'number'` and `Number.isInteger(result)` is true, for all 361 pairs. The concrete rows in Test data table A also hold.
8. AC-8 (C1): Given lower-case or mixed-case input, when it is called, then `notchChange('bbb+','bb+') === 3`, `notchChange('Bb+','bBb+') === -3`, `notchChange('aaa','ccc-') === 18` and `notchChange('a','A') === 0`.

10. AC-10 (C1, C2): Given whitespace that `trim()` keeps, or whitespace inside the rating, when it is called, then `notchChange('\u200BA','A')`, `notchChange('BBB +','A')` and `notchChange('A','B B')` each throw `RangeError`.
11. AC-11 (C2, X-scale-bounds): Given each of `'D'`, `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'SD'`, `'NR'`, `'WD'`, `'AAA+'`, `'A++'`, `'Baa1'`, `'BBB+ (neg)'`, `'BBB+u'`, `'BBB\u2212'` and `'BBB\u2010'`, when it is passed as `previous` (with current `'A'`) and, separately, as `current` (with previous `'A'`), then each of the 26 calls throws `RangeError`, checked with `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`.
12. AC-12 (C2): Given each of `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'` and `'\u00A0'`, when it is passed as `previous` (current `'A'`) and as `current` (previous `'A'`), then each of the 8 calls throws `RangeError`.
13. AC-13 (C2): Given each of `undefined`, `null`, `3`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `[]`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `new String('BBB+')`, `Symbol('A')`, `10n` and `() => 'A'`, when it is passed as `previous` (current `'A'`) and as `current` (previous `'A'`), then each of the 28 calls throws `RangeError`. `notchChange()` and `notchChange('A')` also throw `RangeError`. No call may throw a `TypeError` or return a value.
14. AC-14 (C2, CON-errors): Given both arguments are invalid, when `notchChange('X', null)` and `notchChange('', '')` are called, then each throws `RangeError`. Which argument the error names is not asserted.
15. AC-15 (X-error-message): Given an argument whose string conversion would itself throw, when `notchChange(Object.create(null),'A')`, `notchChange('A',Symbol('x'))` and `notchChange({ toString() { throw new Error('boom') } },'A')` are called, then each throws `RangeError`, not a `TypeError` and not the `Error('boom')`. Also, for `notchChange('D','A')` the caught error's `message` is a non-empty string containing `previous`, and for `notchChange('A','D')` it contains `current`. The exact text is not asserted.
16. AC-16 (C4, ARC-async, CLAUDE.md): Given the repo root as the working directory, when `node --input-type=module -e "import {notchChange} from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'; notchChange('BBB+','BB+'); try{notchChange('D','A')}catch{}"` is run, then it exits `0` with empty stdout and empty stderr. `typeof notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 'number'` (not a Promise). The source of `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, with comments removed, contains no `import` statement, no `import(`, no `require(`, no `console.` and no `process.`.
17. AC-17 (Contract, ARC-stack, CLAUDE.md): Given the finished change, when the repo is inspected, then:
    - `package.json` has no `dependencies` and no `devDependencies` key;
    - `src/ratings/notch.mjs` and `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exist;
    - the test file imports from `'node:test'` and `'node:assert/strict'`;
    - `node --test --test-reporter=tap test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exits `0` with `# tests N`, where N > 0, and `# fail 0`;
    - `npm test` exits `0`.
18. AC-18 (DEL-docs): Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when it is read, then a `/** … */` block comes directly before (only whitespace between) `export const RATING_SCALE`, and another comes directly before `export function notchChange`. The `notchChange` block contains, case-insensitively, `downgrade`, `positive`, `upgrade`, `negative`, `RangeError`, and either `0` or `zero`. `README.md` is byte-identical to `main`.

## Edge cases
- **Signed zero.** The result for any equal pair, including the 19 diagonal pairs of AC-7, must be `+0`. `assert.strictEqual` (node:assert/strict) uses `Object.is`, so a `-0` from `-(prev - cur)` fails AC-3 and AC-7.
- **Loose string checks.** `['A']` and `new String('A')` both turn into `'A'` with `String()`. Both must still throw `RangeError` (AC-13). Only `typeof arg === 'string'` counts as a string.
- **Error type for non-strings.** Every invalid input throws `RangeError`, never `TypeError`. This includes `Symbol`, `BigInt`, functions and a missing argument (C2, PRD-conflicts).
- **Building the message.** A template literal or `+` with a Symbol throws `TypeError`. `String(Object.create(null))` and `String({toString(){throw …}})` throw too. In every one of these cases the error that reaches the caller must still be a `RangeError` (AC-15).
- **Trim rules (exactly `String.prototype.trim()`).** NBSP `\u00A0` and BOM `\uFEFF` at the ends are removed (AC-9). The zero-width space `\u200B` is not removed, so the input is rejected (AC-10). After trimming, a whitespace-only string is empty and is rejected (AC-12).
- **Exact match only.** Prefix, suffix and substring matches are rejected: `'AAA+'`, `'BBB+u'`, `'BBB+ (neg)'`, `'A++'`. A lower-case valid rating such as `'b'` is valid (`notchChange('b','B') === 0`). It is not an invalid case.
- **Look-alike dashes.** U+2212 and U+2010 are not turned into `-`, so those inputs are rejected (AC-11).
- **Scale ends.** `('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `('CCC-','AAA') === -18` are the extreme results. No result is outside -18..+18.
- **Extra arguments are ignored** (plan assumption). `notchChange('A','A','x') === 0`. Unit tests may check this. It is not an AC.
- **The shared scale stays intact.** Mutation attempts in one test (AC-5) must leave the module's `RATING_SCALE` unchanged for every later test in the same process. The module itself never sorts, reverses or otherwise mutates it.
- **Node 18.** The code must not use APIs newer than Node 18, such as `toSorted`, `toReversed`, `Object.groupBy`, Set methods or `isWellFormed`. The local runtime is v22.22.0, so the reviewer checks this by reading the code. QA cannot run Node 18 here.
- **Test discovery.** Both test files end in `.test.mjs` under `test/ratings/`, so bare `node --test` (`npm test`) finds them. QA confirms the reported test count is above 0.

- **Signed zero.** The result for any equal pair, including the 19 diagonal pairs of AC-7, must be `+0`. `assert.strictEqual` (node:assert/strict) uses `Object.is`, so a `-0` from `-(prev - cur)` fails AC-3 and AC-7.

42	## Edge cases
43	- **Signed zero.** The result for any equal pair, including the 19 diagonal pairs of AC-7, must be `+0`. `assert.strictEqual` (node:assert/strict) uses `Object.is`, so a `-0` from `-(prev - cur)` fails AC-3 and AC-7.
44	- **Loose string checks.** `['A']` and `new String('A')` both turn into `'A'` with `String()`. Both must still throw `RangeError` (AC-13). Only `typeof arg === 'string'` counts as a string.
45	- **Error type for non-strings.** Every invalid input throws `RangeError`, never `TypeError`. This includes `Symbol`, `BigInt`, functions and a missing argument (C2, PRD-conflicts).
46	- **Building the message.** A template literal or `+` with a Symbol throws `TypeError`. `String(Object.create(null))` and `String({toString(){throw …}})` throw too. In every one of these cases the error that reaches the caller must still be a `RangeError` (AC-15).
47	- **Trim rules (exactly `String.prototype.trim()`).** NBSP ` ` and BOM `﻿` at the ends are removed (AC-9). The zero-width space `​` is not removed, so the input is rejected (AC-10). After trimming, a whitespace-only string is empty and is rejected (AC-12).
48	- **Exact match only.** Prefix, suffix and substring matches are rejected: `'AAA+'`, `'BBB+u'`, `'BBB+ (neg)'`, `'A++'`. A lower-case valid rating such as `'b'` is valid (`notchChange('b','B') === 0`). It is not an invalid case.
49	- **Look-alike dashes.** U+2212 and U+2010 are not turned into `-`, so those inputs are rejected (AC-11).
50	- **Scale ends.** `('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `('CCC-','AAA') === -18` are the extreme results. No result is outside -18..+18.
51	- **Extra arguments are ignored** (plan assumption). `notchChange('A','A','x') === 0`. Unit tests may check this. It is not an AC.
52	- **The shared scale stays intact.** Mutation attempts in one test (AC-5) must leave the module's `RATING_SCALE` unchanged for every later test in the same process. The module itself never sorts, reverses or otherwise mutates it.
53	- **Node 18.** The code must not use APIs newer than Node 18, such as `toSorted`, `toReversed`, `Object.groupBy`, Set methods or `isWellFormed`. The local runtime is v22.22.0, so the reviewer checks this by reading the code. QA cannot run Node 18 here.
54	- **Test discovery.** Both test files end in `.test.mjs` under `test/ratings/`, so bare `node --test` (`npm test`) finds them. QA confirms the reported test count is above 0.

3	## User story
4	As a developer of Indicators 11–13 and of the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want a pure, synchronous `notchChange(previous, current)` and a frozen `RATING_SCALE` that I can import from `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, so that I get the signed number of notches between two credit ratings (downgrade positive, upgrade negative, no change 0) without writing my own scale lookup.

6	## Traces to
7	AC-1 to AC-18 of plan.md. Requirements: REQ-06-02, C1, C2, C3, C4, Contract. Readiness: CON-interface, CON-errors, X-scale-bounds, X-module-shape, X-error-message, ARC-async, ARC-stack, DEL-docs, TST-strategy, PRD-conflicts.

11	- **Error message (AC-15).** X-error-message fixes only the error type. The integration test may assert that the message is a non-empty string containing `previous` or `current`. Neither unit tests nor integration tests may assert the exact message text.

42	## Edge cases
43	- **Signed zero.** The result for any equal pair, including the 19 diagonal pairs of AC-7, must be `+0`. `assert.strictEqual` (node:assert/strict) uses `Object.is`, so a `-0` from `-(prev - cur)` fails AC-3 and AC-7.
44	- **Loose string checks.** `['A']` and `new String('A')` both turn into `'A'` with `String()`. Both must still throw `RangeError` (AC-13). Only `typeof arg === 'string'` counts as a string.
45	- **Error type for non-strings.** Every invalid input throws `RangeError`, never `TypeError`. This includes `Symbol`, `BigInt`, functions and a missing argument (C2, PRD-conflicts).
46	- **Building the message.** A template literal or `+` with a Symbol throws `TypeError`. `String(Object.create(null))` and `String({toString(){throw …}})` throw too. In every one of these cases the error that reaches the caller must still be a `RangeError` (AC-15).
47	- **Trim rules (exactly `String.prototype.trim()`).** NBSP ` ` and BOM `﻿` at the ends are removed (AC-9). The zero-width space `​` is not removed, so the input is rejected (AC-10). After trimming, a whitespace-only string is empty and is rejected (AC-12).
48	- **Exact match only.** Prefix, suffix and substring matches are rejected: `'AAA+'`, `'BBB+u'`, `'BBB+ (neg)'`, `'A++'`. A lower-case valid rating such as `'b'` is valid (`notchChange('b','B') === 0`). It is not an invalid case.
49	- **Look-alike dashes.** U+2212 and U+2010 are not turned into `-`, so those inputs are rejected (AC-11).
50	- **Scale ends.** `('AAA','CCC-') === 18` and `('CCC-','AAA') === -18` are the extreme results. No result is outside -18..+18.
51	- **Extra arguments are ignored** (plan assumption). `notchChange('A','A','x') === 0`. Unit tests may check this. It is not an AC.
52	- **The shared scale stays intact.** Mutation attempts in one test (AC-5) must leave the module's `RATING_SCALE` unchanged for every later test in the same process. The module itself never sorts, reverses or otherwise mutates it.
53	- **Node 18.** The code must not use APIs newer than Node 18, such as `toSorted`, `toReversed`, `Object.groupBy`, Set methods or `isWellFormed`. The local runtime is v22.22.0, so the reviewer checks this by reading the code. QA cannot run Node 18 here.

+/**
+ * The 19 credit rating scale, from best to worst.
+ * Indices: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9,
+ * BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.
+ * The array is frozen and cannot be modified.
+ */
+export const RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze([
+  'AAA', 'AA+', 'AA', 'AA-', 'A+', 'A', 'A-', 'BBB+', 'BBB', 'BBB-',
+  'BB+', 'BB', 'BB-', 'B+', 'B', 'B-', 'CCC+', 'CCC', 'CCC-'
+])
+
+// Build a map once at module load for O(1) lookup
+const ratingMap = new Map()
+for (let i = 0; i < RATING_SCALE.length; i++) {
+  ratingMap.set(RATING_SCALE[i], i)
+}
+
+/**
+ * Calculate the signed number of notches between two credit ratings.
+ * A downgrade (worse credit) produces a positive result.
+ * An upgrade (better credit) produces a negative result.
+ * No change produces 0.
+ *
+ * Input is normalized by trimming whitespace and matching case-insensitively.
+ * Any invalid input (unknown rating, empty, whitespace-only, or not a string primitive) throws RangeError.
+ *
+ * @param {string} previous - The previous credit rating
+ * @param {string} current - The current credit rating
+ * @returns {number} The signed notch change (current index - previous index)
+ * @throws {RangeError} If either argument is invalid, unknown, or not a string primitive
+ */
+export function notchChange (previous, current) {
+  // Validate and normalize previous
+  const prevIdx = lookupRating(previous, 'previous')
+
+  // Validate and normalize current
+  const currIdx = lookupRating(current, 'current')
+
+  // Return the signed difference (current - previous)
+  return currIdx - prevIdx
+}
+
+/**
+ * Validate and look up a rating string in the scale.
+ * Normalizes by trimming and uppercasing, then performs exact match lookup.
+ *
+ * @param {*} rating - The rating to validate and lookup
+ * @param {string} paramName - The parameter name ('previous' or 'current') for error messages
+ * @returns {number} The index in RATING_SCALE
+ * @throws {RangeError} If the rating is invalid
+ */
+function lookupRating (rating, paramName) {
+  // Check if it's a string primitive (not String object, not other type)
+  if (typeof rating !== 'string') {
+    throw buildRangeError(paramName, rating)
+  }
+
+  // Trim and uppercase
+  const normalized = rating.trim().toUpperCase()
+
+  // Look up in map
+  const idx = ratingMap.get(normalized)
+  if (idx === undefined) {
+    // Unknown or empty rating
+    throw buildRangeError(paramName, rating)
+  }
+
+  return idx
+}
+
+/**
+ * Build a RangeError message safely, handling cases where value conversion might throw.
+ *
+ * @param {string} paramName - The parameter name ('previous' or 'current')
+ * @param {*} value - The invalid value
+ * @returns {RangeError} The error object
+ */
+function buildRangeError (paramName, value) {
+  let description
+
+  try {
+    if (typeof value === 'string') {
+      // For strings, use JSON.stringify for safe representation
+      description = JSON.stringify(value)
+    } else if (typeof value === 'symbol' || typeof value === 'bigint' || typeof value === 'number' || typeof value === 'boolean' || value === undefined) {
+      // For primitives, String() is safe (except for Symbol which we handle separately)
+      if (typeof value === 'symbol') {
+        description = `Symbol`
+      } else {
+        description = String(value)
+      }
+    } else if (value === null) {
+      description = 'null'
+    } else {
+      // For objects/functions, describe by typeof only
+      description = `non-string value of type ${typeof value}`
+    }
+  } catch (e) {
+    // Fallback if anything throws
+    description = `value of type ${typeof value}`
+  }
+
+  const message = `Invalid rating for ${paramName}: ${description}`
+  return new RangeError(message)
+}
